_note: The external competency spine. Registered so every shipped page can name the standard unit it addresses, and so coverage can be MEASURED rather than asserted. Resident spine only at v1 — the student spine (ADMSEP Clinical Learning Objectives Guide, November 2007) is a separate decision recorded on research return rq-1-2026-09-10-2 and is not registered here yet, because its reproduction terms are not established and its DSM-IV-era topic areas need an attributed DSM-5-TR remap first. Nothing here is published while review is 'pending'. rotationRequirement is THIS PROGRAM'S derivation, not an ACGME-published mapping: ACGME publishes no per-rotation milestone subset for psychiatry. Run: python3 bin/check_standards_coverage.py

frameworks.name: ACGME Psychiatry Milestones
frameworks.authority: Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME)
frameworks.note: Implementation date 1 July 2021; page footers also label the report worksheet 'Version 2.1', so both strings appear in the wild — this registry pins the Second Revision March 2020. SBP, PBLI, PROF and ICS here are the harmonized cross-specialty set. No psychiatry-specific revision located after March 2020. ACGME states the Milestones neither represent the entirety of the six domains nor are designed to be relevant in any other context — a fitness-for-purpose scope statement, not a rights restriction, but coverage claims should be worded with it in view.

rights.grantText: ©2020 Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) All rights reserved except the copyright owners grant third parties the right to use the Psychiatry Milestones on a non-exclusive basis for educational purposes.
rights.verifiedVia: Direct fetch of the primary PDF, not a search snippet or a third-party summary. Subcompetency identifiers and titles verified in the same fetch; the count of 21 was confirmed by summing the enumeration (6+4+3+2+3+3), not by trusting a reported total.
rights.pendingQuestion: Open with ACGME (Milestones@ACGME.org, drafted 2026-09-10): (1) does the grant cover reproducing subcompetency identifiers and titles on a public non-commercial educational site; (2) does it extend to the Program Requirements, which carry a copyright line but no located third-party grant. Until (2) is answered, PR clauses are PARAPHRASED, never quoted verbatim on a shipped page. Recorded as RQ-1 finding f3, which is an unverified NEGATIVE of the shape that failed as RQ-10 f3.

units.title: Psychiatric Evaluation
units.rotationRationale: The admission history and MSE is the rotation's core work; PR 4.11.f.1 assigns assessment, diagnosis and treatment to this setting.
units.mappingNote: Risk screening sits here. NOTE the safety-code collision recorded on RQ-1 f4: this is patient RISK, not institutional safety events (SBP1).

units.title: Psychiatric Formulation and Differential Diagnosis
units.rotationRationale: Direct PR 4.11.f.1 deliverable.
units.mappingNote: Maps to every diagnostic code, so it discriminates nothing. Useful as a lattice row, near-useless as a one-to-one map.

units.title: Treatment Planning and Management
units.rotationRationale: Acuity-driven level-of-care decisions are structurally inpatient.
units.mappingNote: Community resources and level-of-care selection are unmapped.

units.title: Psychotherapy
units.rotationRationale: PR 4.11.g.1.a places ongoing individual psychotherapy in the longitudinal outpatient year.
units.mappingNote: CONFIRMED VOCABULARY GAP. Psychotherapy occupies two of 21 subcompetencies and is a hard Program Requirement; the twelve internal codes cannot express it.

units.title: Somatic Therapies
units.rotationRationale: Acute psychopharmacology on an acutely ill inpatient population (PR 1.7.g).
units.mappingNote: Neurostimulation (ECT/TMS) is unmapped.

units.title: Clinical Consultation
units.rotationRationale: PR 4.11.k places consultation-liaison on a separate two-month FTE rotation.
units.mappingNote: Correctly empty for this rotation. This is the canonical example of a gap that is not a gap.

units.title: Development through the Life Cycle
units.rotationRationale: PR 4.11.h (child and adolescent) and 4.11.i (geriatrics) carry the lifespan requirement.
units.mappingNote: Adult and late-life development are unmapped.

units.title: Psychopathology
units.rotationRationale: The varied clinical spectrum requirement (PR 1.7.g) is met here.
units.mappingNote: The best-covered unit in the whole spine. The psychiatry/medicine interface is unmapped.

units.title: Clinical Neuroscience
units.rotationRationale: PR 4.11.e assigns two months FTE of neurology.
units.mappingNote: Weak map: neurodiagnostics and neurological comorbidity are unmapped.

units.title: Psychotherapy
units.rotationRationale: PR 4.11.s places the psychotherapy knowledge base in the didactic curriculum.
units.mappingNote: Second half of the confirmed psychotherapy gap.

units.title: Patient Safety and Quality Improvement
units.rotationRationale: DELIBERATELY UNDECIDED. PR 4.11.q and 6.3 place QI at program level, but restraint reduction and suicide-risk QI are genuinely inpatient activities that the Milestones themselves name. This is the single most defensible place for a program to disagree with the split.
units.mappingNote: MUST NOT be mapped to `safety` — that code means patient risk and this means institutional safety events. Mapping it would manufacture false coverage on the most safety-critical code in the vocabulary. Feeds RQ-2: no QI content exists on either site.

units.title: System Navigation for Patient-Centered Care
units.rotationRationale: Transitions of care and hand-offs live on inpatient units; PR 5.1.k.2.e requires an adequate discharge summary and plan.
units.mappingNote: VOCABULARY GAP: care coordination, transitions, discharge and population health.

units.title: Physician Role in Health Care Systems
units.rotationRationale: PR 4.11.n (community psychiatry) and program-level curriculum.
units.mappingNote: VOCABULARY GAP: health systems, financing, advocacy, transition to practice.

units.title: Evidence-Based and Informed Practice
units.rotationRationale: PR 4.11.s.2 assigns critical appraisal to journal clubs and didactics.
units.mappingNote: VOCABULARY GAP: evidence-based practice and critical appraisal. NOTE the library already has a strong evidence apparatus; the gap is in the CODE vocabulary, not the content.

units.title: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth
units.rotationRationale: PR 5.1.c and 5.1.d assign this to semi-annual CCC review and individualized learning plans.
units.mappingNote: VOCABULARY GAP: reflective practice, feedback, learning plans.

units.title: Professional Behavior and Ethical Principles
units.rotationRationale: Capacity, commitment and involuntary status are enacted on inpatient units; PR 4.11.l content lands here.
units.mappingNote: Clean one-to-one map.

units.title: Accountability/Conscientiousness
units.rotationRationale: Assessed continuously in any patient-care assignment.
units.mappingNote: Partial map.

units.title: Well-Being
units.rotationRationale: PR Section 6 places well-being at institutional and program level.
units.mappingNote: VOCABULARY GAP: physician well-being.

units.title: Patient- and Family-Centered Communication
units.rotationRationale: Family meetings, consent and shared decision-making cluster at admission and discharge.
units.mappingNote: Clean one-to-one map, and the closest unit to this program's family-intervention work.

units.title: Interprofessional and Team Communication
units.rotationRationale: The inpatient multidisciplinary team is the canonical setting; PR 4.11.q requires interdisciplinary team leadership.
units.mappingNote: Partial: interprofessional and team communication are not separable from `relational` as coded.

units.title: Communication within Health Care Systems
units.rotationRationale: Daily notes and the discharge summary; PR 5.1.k.2.a-e monitors clinical records on major rotations.
units.mappingNote: VOCABULARY GAP: documentation.
